newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS WARY OF CELEBRATING TOO SOON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS WARY OF CELEBRATING TOO SOON.

text.p: As far as most people are concerned, Juventus have the Italian league title in their grasp while their rivals are fighting for second place.

That is not entirely how coach Marcello Lippi sees it, despite the pleasure of seeing a depleted Juventus easily overcome Vicenza 2-0 at home on Saturday to build up a commanding seven point lead in serie A.

The European Cup holders have a tiring week ahead of them, with a trip to Norway for a cup quarter-final first leg match against Rosenborg on Wednesday and a top of the table league clash against Inter in Milan on Sunday.

On paper, the Norwegian part-timers are the weakest opponents Juventus could have drawn although they managed to knock AC Milan out at the Champions' League stage despite having lost heavily to them in their meeting in Norway.

Inter are far more dangerous, having thrashed Juventus 3-0 in Milan in the Italian Cup in November. That remains the heaviest defeat Juventus have suffered this season with the Turin team unbeaten in the European Cup so far.
"If we go to Milan on Sunday and lose, then we have just four points advantage and the championship is re-opened with the usual debate, the same tired old phrases," said Lippi.
"We need balance. I don't feel I can declare the championship to be closed and I certainly don't want anyone to misinterpret my analysis of the situation."

That said, Lippi praised his men for what he said had constituted an extraordinary performance in the circumstances, with regulars Alessandro Del Piero and Croat Alen Boksic injured and Frenchman Zinedine Zidane disqualified for one match.
French midfielder Didier Deschamps, who was also injured, should be back in time for Rosenborg but Boksic, who last played on January 12, is likely to remain an absentee.
Juventus fly to Trondheim on Tuesday and the Croat may not even be on the plane.
"He's not ready and in the cup I can only take five substitutes with me," said Lippi, who will also have to make do without Del Piero until the end of the month.

In the absence of the leading lights, Italy midfielder Angelo Di Livio and Striker Michele Padovano scored the goals for a revamped Juventus team that still looked in a different class to their Italian Cup finalist opponents.
"I don't see them slacking off at all but I believe it would be a mistake to consider a certain situation to be resolved when it is still far from being over," Lippi said.
"The fact is that people are celebrating when we have not yet won anything. We must keep our calm."

The daily Tuttosport newspaper carried a front page editorial headlined "Desperately seeking rivals" while the Gazzetta dello Sport's main headline on Monday was "Juventus is laughing" over another declaring "Lippi is the boss".

Saturday's tidy victory, with a goal in each half and Juventus always in control of the pace of the game, was all the more impressive because it showed clearly that the Turin club has a far stronger team spirit than most.
It was not a great team on display but greatness is relative and at the moment there are few clubs in Italy that can come close to Juventus even when they are below par.
A record 24th league title and the possible retention of the European Cup would be an extraordinary way for the club to celebrate its 100th birthday in November.
